input: Research remote island campsites for summer

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Remote island camping varies enormously by region — Pacific Northwest, Caribbean, Southeast Asia, Scandinavia, etc. — and the right region changes every recommendation.
Solo, couple, family with kids, or group trip changes site suitability, safety requirements, and logistics completely.
The specific month or window within summer affects ferry/boat availability, permit seasons, weather windows, and booking lead times.
Remote island camping can range from free primitive sites to expensive charter-access-only locations; budget shapes which options are even relevant.
Whether the user can handle a kayak paddle-in, a water taxi, a charter boat, or needs a ferry determines which islands are viable.
A true wilderness/primitive camping experience versus a site with basic amenities changes the shortlist of islands entirely.
Knowing whether the output should be a curated shortlist, a comparison table, booking links, or a full trip plan defines what 'done well' looks like.

gold.taskTitle: Research remote island campsites for summer
gold.taskDescription: Find and evaluate remote island camping options for a summer trip.

questions.title: Which region or country should the islands be in?
questions.description: Identify the geographic area — e.g., Pacific Northwest, Scandinavia, Caribbean, Southeast Asia — to narrow the search to relevant campsites.

questions.title: How many people are going on this trip?
questions.description: Determine group size and composition (solo, couple, family, friend group) to match site capacity and suitability.

questions.title: Which specific weeks or month in summer are you targeting?
questions.description: Pin down the travel window to align with permit availability, weather conditions, and booking deadlines.

questions.title: What is your total budget for the camping trip?
questions.description: Establish a budget range to filter out sites that require expensive charters or paid permits beyond what the user can spend.

questions.title: How do you expect to reach the island — kayak, ferry, or charter?
questions.description: Clarify the mode of access the user is willing or able to use, which determines which remote islands are physically reachable.

questions.title: Do you want primitive wilderness sites or basic amenities?
questions.description: Understand whether the user wants true backcountry camping or sites with toilets, fire rings, or potable water to refine the shortlist.

questions.title: What should the final research output actually look like?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants a curated shortlist, a comparison table, direct booking links, or a full itinerary plan so the deliverable matches expectations.
